title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When we one-hot encode a categorical variable, we create a binary column for each category. For example, if we one-hot encode the 'sex' column, we will have two new columns: $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$.

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: The design matrix \( \Phi_2 \) includes one-hot encoded columns for 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$, as well as an intercept term. How many columns does this result in?

title: Counting One-Hot Encoded Columns
text: How many columns are created by one-hot encoding the 'sex' column?

title: Counting One-Hot Encoded Columns for $$'embark_{town'}$$

title: Total Columns in \( \Phi_2 \)
text: Including the intercept term, how many columns are there in total in \( \Phi_2 \)?

title: Invertibility of \( \Phi_2**{T}\Phi_2 \)
text: For a matrix to be invertible, it must be square and have full rank. Consider the number of rows and columns in \( \Phi_2 \).
